title: Web Components: custom elements, shadow DOM and templates

videos.script:
The planner's components are functions that return elements. A React app cannot use them as they are, and neither can Angular, Vue or Svelte, without a wrapper each.

{{standard}} The browser has its own answer, three standards that together are called Web Components. A tag you define yourself. A private tree of elements that the page's CSS cannot reach. And a template you clone instead of building by hand.

{{element}} You will write one, planner-session, in the library from lesson 7. It reads its attributes, draws a row, and announces when it is marked done.

{{boundary}} Then the boundary. The demo page paints every button red, and the component's button stays green, because the shadow root keeps the page out. The tokens still get in, and you will see why.

{{tests}} Playwright then checks all of it, through the boundary, and axe checks the result.

{{frameworks}} And the same tag, used from each of the four frameworks, side by side.
